raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes the Rust TreeCore gap in #41579. Mirrors #41580's `_maybe_split_for_window_lock` in the native Rust TreeCore: a lock walk that reaches a long live-SWA ancestor now splits it to a page-aligned window tail (default-on `SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY`) instead of pinning it whole. #40283 is complementary rather than a replacement. Regression test: 7-token endpoint + 32-token live ancestor + 8-token window pins 8 tokens (was 39) and unlocks cleanly. 868 lib tests pass.

AI-assisted (code written with AI help).

nodes.body:
Thanks @apex-mochen. I read the diff against #41580's Python and built it here (`e727eb7`, Rust 1.92, torch 2.11): the lib suite is 923 passed, and the new test fails against the merge-base's `swa.rs` (the ancestor stays 32 tokens), so it reproduces. The split matches the Python: the same guards (unlocked, live on device, not write-through pending), the same page-aligned tail and alignment check, the original id kept as the tail, device walk only. The release walk still ends at the uuid-stamped tail, so lock and release cover the same segment. The changed expectations in `acquire_lock_overshooting_the_window_stops_at_the_crossing_node` are the intended effect (the crossing node now pins only its in-window tail); the Python walk does the same there.

Two small things:
1. `swa_lock_window_only()` doesn't parse the flag the way Python's `EnvBool` does. With `SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY=no` (or `n`) both tests above still pass here, so the Rust split stays on, while Python reads `no` as false and turns its split off; `off` disables it here but is an error in Python. `sglang-server`'s `utils/environ.rs::env_bool` already mirrors `EnvBool.parse`; matching it would switch both TreeCores with the same values.
2. It's read on every iteration of the walk; the Python reads it once before the loop (`window_only = not lock_host and envs.SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY.get()`). Hoisting it would match and saves a getenv per node.

Thanks for the build verification @bill-h-lin — matching the merge-base failure for the new test is exactly the regression coverage I was aiming for.

The CI matrix on this PR is still gated: `call-gate` requires the `run-ci` label, which turns the `pr-test-*-finish` aggregate jobs red (everything else is skipped). Could you add `run-ci` (or run `/tag-run-ci-label`) when you get a chance? Happy to address anything that comes up in the platform runs.

Thanks @bill-h-lin — both fixed in 7ba21bd4, as a delta on top of the `e727eb7` you built so the re-review is just that one commit.

**1. EnvBool parity.** `SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY` now goes through a local `env_bool` with Python `EnvBool.parse`'s literal sets (`true/1/yes/y`, `false/0/no/n`, anything else invalid → default), so `no`/`n` turn the split off as they do in Python and `off` — not a Python literal — keeps the default instead of disabling it. I replicated the parse rather than calling `sglang-server`'s `utils::environ::env_bool` because `rust/Cargo.toml` excludes `sglang-radix-tree` from the root workspace, so that crate isn't reachable from here; the literal sets are pinned by a unit test (unique var names, the same trick `environ.rs`'s own test uses, since tests share the process env).

**2. Hoisted.** `let window_only = !lock_host && Self::swa_lock_window_only();` sits above the loop now, mirroring the Python line you quoted.

Behaviour, with the flag as the only variable (lib suite, Rust 1.92):

| `SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY` | result |
| --- | --- |
| unset | 924 passed (923 + the new parse test) |
| `no` | 922 passed, 2 failed — the two split tests, i.e. the split is genuinely off now (it used to stay on here) |
| `off` | 924 passed — invalid in Python, so the default keeps the split on |

`cargo fmt --check` and `clippy` are clean. Note the two split-behaviour tests assume the flag is unset; that is now stated in the test file next to the parse test.

Thanks @apex-mochen, and you're right about `off`: `EnvBool.parse` rejects it, but `EnvField.get` catches that, warns and keeps the default, so keeping the split on matches Python. My note had that wrong.

Re-checked at 7ba21bd (Rust 1.92): the lib suite gives 924 with the flag unset, `off` or `y`, and 922 with `0`, `no`, `n` or `false` (the two split tests, as expected). I also ran #41580's Python test through SGLang's own source build of the Rust TreeCore (the shared suite with the backend set to `rust`, on CPU): on main's Rust it fails in every SWA configuration it runs in (8, page sizes 1 to 128), and with this PR's `swa.rs` it passes, with the flag on and off via `envs.SGLANG_SWA_LOCK_WINDOW_ONLY.override`. Across the whole shared suite this PR fixes exactly those 8 and changes nothing else that runs on CPU.

On CI: I can't add `run-ci` or use `/tag-run-ci-label`, since I'm not in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`. @ispobock @xiezhq-hermann, could one of you tag this one? #41580 will follow once its rebase is pushed: `test_rust_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` reruns its test on the Rust core too, so the two should land together or this one first.

Hi @bill-h-lin — thanks for the second verification (7ba21bd4, EnvBool parity + split behavior settled). The PR is still gated: `call-gate` needs the `run-ci` label before the platform matrix can execute. Could you add it when you have a moment so the Rust companion can be validated on the full CI? Happy to rebase again if anything drifts.

@apex-mochen I can't add it: neither of us is in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so the label has to come from someone on that list. @Jialin @alphabetc1, you own `rust/sglang-radix-tree`; could one of you add `run-ci`?

Since my last note I've also run the shared suite on the Rust core with the GPU visible, which covers the 398 tests my CPU runs couldn't (they need CUDA streams; mostly HiCache transfers). The tree was #41580's rebased branch (`f6bd8ab61f`, on main `a34cba3c62`; main's `swa.rs` hasn't changed since). With main's Rust the only failures are #41580's 8 SWA cases; with this PR's `swa.rs` at `7ba21bd`, all 1,306 tests that run pass. #41580 is pushed, so the two can land together, or this one first.

@apex-mochen one more thing, found while rebasing #41580 onto today's `main` (`0b635266d4`). #42633 (merged 10-06) added buffer-mode HiCache backups. The buffer pipeline pins a node with `inc_lock_ref` when it launches the D2H copy, and that pin is itself a lock walk, so the window-only split fires on the node being written: its older part is no longer pinned until the ack, and the written keys no longer match the node. On the Python core, #42633's `test_buffer_only_writes_component_pools_independently` caught it with #41580's flag on, and #41580 now leaves a node whole while `buffer_backup_pending(node.id)` (pushed as `4dad756d38`).

The same happens on the Rust core with this PR, and CI won't show it: that test forces the Python core (it overrides a component). I ran its flow with the default components (insert one window + 1 page, back up the leaf through the buffer pipeline, drain), on GPU:

| | node split by the backup's pin | writes match the chain |
|---|---|---|
| Rust, `main` | 0 / 8 configurations | 8 / 8 |
| Rust, this PR at `7ba21bd` | 6 / 8 (all page sizes > 1; e.g. 384 → 128 tokens at page size 128) | 2 / 8 |
| Python, #41580 with the check | 0 / 8 | 8 / 8 |
| Python, #41580 without it | the same 6 / 8 | 2 / 8 |

The Rust core can't see the pipeline's pending set (`BufferModePipeline.inflight_backup_pools`, Python-side), so a guard needs that state passed down, e.g. the adapter marks a node when the pipeline enqueues it and clears it at the ack, and the split skips marked nodes, as the Python side does. A blunter option is to skip the split under `is_host_memory_buffer_only`. Your call; I'm happy to re-run this on whatever you push. As a test for the shared suite (it runs on both cores there):

<details><summary>test</summary>

```python
    def test_buffer_backup_pin_does_not_split_the_node_it_writes(self):
        self._skip_unsupported_hicache_test()
        storage_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, storage_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        cache, allocator, req_to_token_pool = build_fixture(self.cfg)
        self._init_buffer_hicache(cache, storage_dir)
        seq = self._buffer_swa_seq()
        self._insert(cache, allocator, req_to_token_pool, seq)
        leaf = cache.match_prefix(
            MatchPrefixParams(key=RadixKey(array("q", seq)))
        ).last_device_node
        chain = self._path_chain(cache, leaf)
        before = [_node_key_length(cache, n) for n in chain]
        controller = cache.cache_controller
        with mock.patch.object(
            controller, "write_storage", wraps=controller.write_storage
        ) as write_storage:
            _write_backup(cache, leaf)
            self._pump_hicache_until(
                cache,
                lambda: (
                    not cache.buffer_pipeline.inflight_backup_node_ids
                    and not cache.buffer_pipeline.ongoing_backup
                ),
                "buffer backup pipeline did not drain",
            )
        self.assertEqual([_node_key_length(cache, n) for n in chain], before)
        kv_writes = {
            tuple(c.args[2]) for c in write_storage.call_args_list if c.args[2]
        }
        self.assertEqual(
            kv_writes, {tuple(cache.tree_core.get_hash_values(n)) for n in chain}
        )
```

</details>

@apex-mochen thanks, verified at `ca3498f` on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120). My split check from above now splits in 0 / 8 configurations, and in 6 / 8 with only `|| node.buffer_backup_pending` removed, so it reaches your guard. Your new shared test passes in its 13 configurations and fails in those same 6 without the guard. The shared suite on both cores, with the GPU, adds no failure over `main` `0b635266d4`. Paired with #41580 (`4dad756d38`), nothing splits on either core. The pending mirror matches `inflight_backup_pools` at both of its edit points. Nothing further from me.

Thanks @bill-h-lin for verifying `ca3498f` on the RTX PRO 6000 — the 0/8 vs 6/8 split counts confirm the buffer-mode backup node is now kept whole across the lock walk.

On CI: the platform matrix on this head is still gated — `call-gate` fails without the `run-ci` label (jobs skipped, so no real platform run yet). Waiting on an owner from `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` (@Jialin or @alphabetc1) to tag it; happy to rebase again if anything drifts.

Hi @Jialin @alphabetc1, following up on #42745.

@bill-h-lin has independently verified the latest fix on an RTX PRO 6000, including the buffer-mode regression and shared tests across both cores, with no remaining findings from that review.

The platform CI is still gated by the external-contributor authorization check. Could an authorized maintainer help enable CI and advise whether anything else is needed for final review?

Happy to address any remaining issues. Thanks!

Hi @Jialin @alphabetc1, just a brief follow-up on the CI authorization for #42745.

The latest fix at ca3498f has been independently validated on GPU by @bill-h-lin, with no remaining findings from that review.

The remaining step appears to be enabling the platform CI and obtaining final code-owner review.

Could one of you help with the run-ci label when convenient, or point me to the appropriate maintainer?

Thanks for your time!

Root cause of the platform failures found and fixed.

The `set_buffer_backup_pending` binding added for the buffer-mode feedback used the legacy `py.allow_threads` API, which does not exist on the pyo3 version the platform builds compile against — `main` has migrated every other binding in this file to `py.detach`. The rust extension failed to compile (E0599 at python_bindings.rs:1869), which cascaded into the AMD/NPU test failures (servers could not start).

Pushed `a0455a03` aligning the binding with the rest of the file (`py.detach(|| self.core().set_buffer_backup_pending(...))`). Same closure, same GIL-release semantics, no behavior change.

Platform rust-ext builds should compile again now. Could a maintainer trigger a CI rerun (or add the run-ci label)? Thanks @Jialin @alphabetc1.

Thanks for adding run-ci on #42745 — the platform matrix is running now. I'm going through the two failing partitions (scripted SWA stash-gate assert + deepseek_v41 score) to confirm whether they're flaky infra or something in the change; will update shortly.

The buffer pipeline pins a node with `inc_lock_ref` when it launches the D2H copy, and that pin is itself a lock walk, so the window-only split fires on the node being written: its older part is no longer pinned until the ack, and the written keys no longer match the node. On the Python core, #42633's `test_buffer_only_writes_component_pools_independently` caught it with #41580's flag on, and #41580 now leaves a node whole while `buffer_backup_pending(node.id)` (pushed as `4dad756d38`).

The same happens on the Rust core with this PR, and CI won't show it: that test forces the Python core (it overrides a component). I ran its flow with the default components (insert one window + 1 page, back up the leaf through the buffer pipeline, drain), on GPU:

| | node split by the backup's pin | writes match the chain |
|---|---|---|
| Rust, `main` | 0 / 8 configurations | 8 / 8 |
| Rust, this PR at `7ba21bd` | 6 / 8 (all page sizes > 1; e.g. 384 → 128 tokens at page size 128) | 2 / 8 |
| Python, #41580 with the check | 0 / 8 | 8 / 8 |
| Python, #41580 without it | the same 6 / 8 | 2 / 8 |

The Rust core can't see the pipeline's pending set (`BufferModePipeline.inflight_backup_pools`, Python-side), so a guard needs that state passed down, e.g. the adapter marks a node when the pipeline enqueues it and clears it at the ack, and the split skips marked nodes, as the Python side does. A blunter option is to skip the split under `is_host_memory_buffer_only`. Your call; I'm happy to re-run this on whatever you push. As a test for the shared suite (it runs on both cores there):

Root cause of the platform failures found and fixed.

The `set_buffer_backup_pending` binding added for the buffer-mode feedback used the legacy `py.allow_threads` API, which does not exist on the pyo3 version the platform builds compile against — `main` has migrated every other binding in this file to `py.detach`. The rust extension failed to compile (E0599 at python_bindings.rs:1869), which cascaded into the AMD/NPU test failures (servers could not start).

Pushed `a0455a03` aligning the binding with the rest of the file (`py.detach(|| self.core().set_buffer_backup_pending(...))`). Same closure, same GIL-release semantics, no behavior change.
